title: Protoplast Isolation from Zymoseptoria tritici
author: Haseena Khan
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k2mcyc6

steps.title: Prepare Zymoseptoria tritici culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate Zymoseptoria tritici into Potato Dextrose Broth (PDB) and incubate at 22°C with 130 rpm shaking.

substeps.instruction: Option 1: Inoculate 100µl dense spore suspension into 500 ml PDB.
Option 2: Inoculate 50µl dense spore suspension into 100ml PDB.

steps.title: Collect spores
steps.instruction: On the fourth day of culture, collect the spores via centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Pour 50 ml of Zymo culture into a 50 mL falcon tube and centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Pour off supernatant.
Repeat the process with a second 50 mL of Zymo culture.

steps.title: Wash pellet with sterile water
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 50ml of sterile water by shaking the tube, then centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4°C and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Wash pellet with Sorbitol
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 40 ml of 1 M Sorbitol by shaking, then centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 10 minutes at 4°C and pour off the supernatant.

steps.title: Digest cell walls
steps.instruction: Treat the pellet with glucanase enzyme and incubate.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.35 g glucanase enzyme to 25 ml of filter sterilized glucanex solution and add this to the pellet.
Shake the tube gently to dissolve the pellet and pour the mixture into a sterile plastic petri dish.
Incubate for 1 hour 40 minutes at 28°C without shaking.

steps.title: Isolate protoplast interface
steps.instruction: Separate the digested sample using a density gradient centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Carefully pour the digested sample from the petri plate into a 50 ml falcon tube.
Gently overlay the sample with 5 ml of 600 mM Sorbitol + 10 mM Tris (pH 7.5) using a 1000 µl pipette tip, pouring against the wall of the tube to avoid mixing.
Centrifuge at 4000 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully collect the interface layer (avoiding the bottom layer) using a 1000 µl pipette and transfer to a 15ml falcon tube.
Add an equal amount of 1M Sorbitol + 10 mM Tris (pH 7.5) to the top and mix gently by tilting the tube slowly.

steps.title: Filter and concentrate protoplasts
steps.instruction: Filter the solution and pellet the protoplasts, keeping tubes on ice from this point forward.

substeps.instruction: Pour the solution over autoclaved cotton wool in a sterile syringe (without piston) and allow it to drip slowly into a 15 ml falcon tube.
Centrifuge at 1500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant with a 1000 µl pipette without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Wash and standardize protoplast suspension
steps.instruction: Wash the protoplasts and adjust the concentration in STC buffer (1.2 M Sorbitol, 10 mM CaCl2, 10 mM Tris pH 7.5).

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of STC buffer, centrifuge at 1500 g for 5 min at 4°C, and carefully remove the supernatant.
Gently resuspend the protoplasts in 500 µl of STC buffer by tapping the tube with fingers.
Take 10µl of the solution and count in a hemocytometer.
Dilute with STC buffer to a final concentration of 1 x 10^6 protoplasts/ml.
Use 100-200 µl of these freshly isolated protoplasts for transformation.

steps.title: Verify protoplast purity
steps.instruction: Perform a bursting test under a microscope to confirm the presence of protoplasts.

substeps.instruction: Place a drop of the protoplast suspension on a slide and examine under a microscope to visualize round protoplasts.
Add a drop of sterile water to the side of the slide without disturbing the coverslip.
Confirm that protoplasts burst upon the addition of water, while intact cells or debris remain.
